summary:
Technical review of phase:f-compensation, iteration 1 (sub-mv44juz3-01ac72c7; commit aab23e6, tree a9aba38c; 61 artifacts, all unchanged on disk; no code change since aab23e6). I read the full src diff bf1a723..HEAD: saga.js, reconciler.js, calls.js, admin.js and routes/admin.js (+219/-39), and the f3 public diff, and checked them against the spec: provider call protocol 1-7, the payment saga steps 1-6, the reconciler, Admin routes and derivation row 2. I re-ran all four plan commands verbatim:
- f1: 40/40 (ev:ev-mv44zcfv-01cfa3ef).
- f2: 56/56 (ev:ev-mv44ztri-017e5d46).
- f3: 205/205 (ev:ev-mv44zv7u-010f184d).
- f4 under the suite lock: the first run had one failure, the known FU-33 race (ev:ev-mv451ngy-01bf3721). The single re-run allowed by dec-mv3tqbn4-01d43152 passed: npm test 2267 tests, 2259 pass, 0 fail, 8 skipped; NFR5 p95 65.7 ms; browser 14/14, with RS-17 and RS-32(a) at 360 and 1280 (ev:ev-mv455hce-01858e59).

**Mutation.** I ran 9 mutants of my own on phase F logic, each in a fresh directory with its diff kept (ev:ev-mv45c3hv-0174ae15; sources ev:ev-mv45fn0w-015fc010). 7 are killed. Of the two survivors, MF6 is equivalent by construction and MF4 is reachable only inside the window before a regular reconciler tick (TR-F-5). MF3, the unbounded reset pass, is killed only by a hang (TR-F-2).

**Correctness.** RS-13, RS-15, RS-17, RS-22, RS-26, RS-32(a), RS-37, RS-38, F-TR-2, F-TR-6 and F-TR-7 conform as tested, and so do the F follow-ups FU-36, FU-38, FU-41, FU-42, FU-43 and FU-45.

**FU-49 does not conform to the spec's intent: TR-F-1, major.** My reproduction probe (ev:ev-mv455seu-01b2f7c0) shows the following:
- once the reconciler's read has restored the operation to `authorized` and the reads then fail, the plan is taken over every tick (epoch 2 -> 10 over 8 ticks) with two reads per tick and no send;
- after 20 minutes the buyer still reads 'Payments are being captured' / WAIT, and no escalation follows. The same outage with the operation still `unknown` escalates at 15 minutes and keeps the epoch at 1.

**Other findings.**
- TR-F-2 (minor): the SEC-11 bound test can only hang.
- TR-F-3 (minor): two LIVE-P1 labels and RISK-18's title overstate the live coverage.
- TR-F-4 (minor): the rejected-refund mapping is pinned suite-wide only by rework-5's admin-basic test; the compensation-path consequence is untested.
- TR-F-5, TR-F-6 and TR-F-7 are info.

SECURITY: PENDING (folded in when the security draft is FINAL).

findings.title: FU-49: the FU-41(a) hold path repeats the takeover every tick while the holder's read fails, and the stuck plan never escalates
findings.recommendation:
Owner: backend-engineer (f2 owns saga.js and reconciler.js; src/domain/derive.js has no phase F owner, so the orchestrator scopes a rework if that file is chosen).

Resolved when both of the following hold:

(a) **The stuck state escalates.** With the holder's read failing for longer than RS_UNKNOWN_ESCALATE_MIN, the request reads `failed_needs_attention` (row 2), with a test. Either option is acceptable:
- On a failed or held holder read, the operation goes back to `unknown` (prev_status `authorized`, the original unknown_since kept), so the existing F-TR-7 takeover exclusion and row 2 apply unchanged. This is my preferred fix: it also stops the epoch growth.
- Or derivation row 2 escalates on a capture call `unknown` for longer than RS_UNKNOWN_ESCALATE_MIN.

(b) **The epoch is settled.** Either the same test shows that lease_epoch no longer grows per tick in this state, or an orchestrator decision accepts the per-tick takeover with its rationale and the verification report states it.

The FU-41(a) tests and lost-response stay green, the full suite passes under the lock, and my probe's expectations flip: the epoch stays bounded and the status escalates.

findings.title: SEC-11 'the pass is bounded' can only hang, never fail, when the bound is removed
findings.detail:
admin-reset.test.js L219 makes the provider's reads never resolve, awaits resetDemo, and only then asserts `elapsed < 5000`.

With the budget removed (my MF3; f2's M-reset-unbounded, 'pass 4 fail 0'), the await never returns. My runner killed the mutant only through its own 90 s --test-timeout ('cancelled 1, fail 0'; ev:ev-mv45c3hv-0174ae15). npm test sets no per-test timeout, so this regression would stall the whole suite until the evidence run's 1800 s limit, instead of reporting a red test.
findings.recommendation: Owner: backend-engineer (f2's file), at the next touch of admin-reset.test.js, or as a phase G test item. Resolved when the test bounds its own wait, for example with `{ timeout: 10_000 }` on the test or a Promise.race against a timer with an assertion, and an unbounded-pass mutant shows a red assertion (fail >= 1) within that time.

findings.title: Two 'LIVE-P1 fact' labels and RISK-18's title claim live coverage that no live test provides
findings.detail:
The submission's criteria table says:
- RS-21: 'the live DENIED/PENDING semantics are LIVE-P1 facts';
- F-TR-6: 'PayPal's answer to a void after capture is a LIVE-P1 fact'.

LIVE-P1 is RS-18/19/20/23/24 (plan.json). None of the live files (test/live/paypal: rs18, rs19, rs20, rs23, rs24, journey-sandbox) exercises an authorization DENIED or PENDING, or a void after capture. So these facts stay unverified even after the user's LIVE-P1 run.

RISK-18's title reads 'live RS-19/20/22/23/24 evidence', but the spec's evidence table (spec.md, Testing: RS-22 row) makes RS-22 [D] only, and no live RS-22 file exists or is planned.

The 'Fake only' column itself is honest. followups.md item 18 already lists the facts as LIVE-DEPENDENT and flags RISK-18.

findings.title: Rejected-refund mapping: suite-wide regression cover exists only in rework-5's admin-basic; the compensation-path consequence is untested
findings.detail:
**Is the current cover enough?** For the mapping itself, yes:
- since rework-5 iteration 2, admin-basic.test.js L407-L408 pins `refund_failed` and INVALID_RESOURCE_ID;
- my kill-check on this same tree (ev:ev-mv44wbl4-0121944a, tree a9aba38c) shows the mutant MB (calls.js L296 -> 'refunded') red.

**What is still untested** is what f2 owns downstream. In compensation (saga step 5), a refund the provider rejects must keep the reservation `reconciling`, escalate it, and never restock. Under MB the release check would restock and release while the money stays captured. capture-compensation covers only the FAILED-status 200 answer (calls.js L290-L291).

**Origin.** f2's handoff (remaining issue 1) proposed asserting 'only that one call exists' in admin-basic. That suggestion produced the TR-R5-1 gap; rework-5 corrected it.

findings.title: Two of my mutants survived: MF6 is equivalent, MF4 is reachable only before a regular reconciler tick
findings.detail:
**MF6** (saga.js L257, the empty-plan guard of releaseIfSettled, removed): any reset closes every `reconciling` reservation in the same transaction that archives the operations (admin.js closedReconciling). So no `reconciling` reservation with only archived operations can reach the release check. The guard is defensive, and the mutant is equivalent.

**MF4** (the reset pass skips 'stale started intents -> unknown'): a started intent becomes stale after 2 x RS_PAYPAL_TIMEOUT_MS (40 s), and every reconciler tick (15 s) marks it anyway. Only a stale intent the regular tick has not yet marked (at most one interval) would be missed by the forced reset, and it would then be listed as stranded rather than resolved.

No change is needed for this gate.
findings.recommendation: No change required. Optional, owner f2 or phase G: a forced-reset test with a stale started void intent would pin MF4. Resolved by the verification report listing both survivors with this reasoning.

findings.title: A forced reset does not fence a live executing saga; a capture in flight can land after the archive, and its stranded entry then shows a stale status
findings.detail:
settleForForcedReset queues voids for `authorized` operations of executing plans and runs a pass of up to 30 s outside any transaction. Meanwhile the plan's lease holder may still start a capture: the capture guard (saga.js sendCapture) checks the lease and `authorized`, not cancel_requested_at. Nothing in the reset changes lease_epoch.

If a capture lands after the archiving transaction:
- its result is recorded on the archived row;
- the refund that the cancellation hook queues is never sent, because startCall refuses archived operations;
- the `stranded` entry reported to the operator says `authorized`, while PayPal shows the authorization CAPTURED.

The readResolvePass deadline has a similar tail: a read in flight when the budget expires finishes, and is recorded after the archive.

The reset is demo-only, admin-only, needs force plus a reason, and spends Sandbox money. SEC-11 accepts manual clean-up for whatever is stranded.
findings.recommendation: No change required for this gate. Owner: delivery-lead (verification report, item 16). Resolved when the report states that the `stranded` statuses are as of the archive, and that a capture in flight for an executing plan can complete after it (check the authorization in the Sandbox dashboard). Optionally, the archive transaction could bump lease_epoch of executing plans to fence late result writes.

findings.title: FU-33: the race is in the test, not in contention; raise it to the first phase G item
findings.recommendation: Owner: orchestrator (FU-33, dec-mv3tqbn4-01d43152). Make it the first phase G change, before any further full-suite evidence is gathered. Resolved when the test waits for the file as well as the row (the one-line fix) and three consecutive locked npm test runs pass it.
